**Source map — OECD Economic Survey: Mexico 2022 (Chapter 2, extract pp. 102–127)**

*Source role:* International organisation (OECD), policy synthesis. Period coverage primarily 2017–2020, with some 2021 data; charter dated February 2022.

### Atomic claims (5B-relevant)

| # | Claim | Locator (page/fig/table) | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Digital government: 25% of Mexico's population used internet to interact with public authorities in 2019; Estonia rose from 50% (2009) to 80% (2019). | p.102 ¶1, citing OECD 2020 [61] | Observed fact (Mex.), international comparison |
| 2 | Digital diffusion lags: large education, age, and income gaps; >70% of older adults (55–74) in Mexico do NOT use internet vs. 40% OECD avg non-users (i.e. 60% OECD use vs <30% MX). | p.103 ¶1, Fig.2.21–2.22 | Observed (ENDUTIH 2020; OECD DEO 2020) |
| 3 | Business digitalisation: ~9% of Mexican firms purchased cloud services vs ~32% OECD; 35% of firms accept digital payments (57% retail); IoT penetration "one of the lowest." | p.105 ¶2, Figs. 2.24–2.26 | Observed (ENAFIN 2018; OECD DEO 2020) |
| 4 | ICT task intensity of jobs "ranks low" with "large regional disparities." | p.107, Fig.2.27 (PIAAC 2018) | Observed |
| 5 | Digital payments: ~1/3 of adults made ≥1 digital payment in 2017 vs ~2/3 in Chile; 55% of credit-card holders used cards in 2019; cash used for 90% of small, 78% of large payments; regional concentrations in CDMX, Quintana Roo, Northern states. | p.108 ¶1, Fig.2.13 (ENIF 2018; CNBV 2020) | Observed |
| 6 | Payment-card market: 5 largest banks ≈80% share (Bátiz-Zuk & Lara Sánchez 2021); single domestic open system run by Asociación de Bancos de México; 4 clearing houses authorised — Prosa (Banorte, Santander, HSBC, Scotiabank), E-Global (BBVA, CITIBANAMEX), Visa MX, Mastercard MX (latter two not yet operational). | p.109 ¶2, Box 2.5; p.110 ¶1 | Observed + interpretation; antitrust risk flagged by OECD |
| 7 | Fintech Law (2018) slow authorisation: as of mid-Oct 2021, of ~76 applicants in payments/crowdfunding, 17 fully authorised and 37 conditionally; online financial frauds = 70% of all financial frauds in Q1 2021. | p.110 ¶2 | Observed |
| 8 | CoDi (Banxico launch Nov 2019): only ~10% of fixed-broadband users know it; ~2% have used it (IFT 2021). | p.111 ¶1 | Observed |
| 9 | Identity: 89% of Mexican adults hold identity document (Global Findex 2017), vs 98% (Costa Rica, Brazil, Peru), 99% (Chile); RENAPO reports 0.8% of population lacks ID (INEGI 2015); 2020 government created digital identity & digital National Population Registry — "should be operative within the next two years." | p.112 ¶1 | Observed + implementation claim (not yet realised) |
| 10 | CNBV digital onboarding: 2020 simplified rule (extended to corporates + SOFIPOs); September 2021 extended to brokerage houses, investment funds, small banks, credit unions. | p.112 ¶2 | Official reform (de jure) |
| 11 | Adult skills (PIAAC 2018): Mexico high-proficiency shares — Literacy 0.8%, Numeracy 0.7%, Problem Solving 10%; OECD means 10/11/30%; ~39% of Mexican adults lack very basic computer skills; ~1% achieve high proficiency across all three. | p.114, Table 2.1, Box 2.8 | Observed |
| 12 | Regional cognitive-skill gap: CDMX & Northern states best; informal workers score below formal workers; among trained informal workers ~50% employer-funded vs 85% formal. | p.115, Figs. 2.29–2.30 | Observed |
| 13 | Digital skills programmes: MexicoX (>230 courses, >1.5 M users); @prende.mx (schools, teacher platforms, pilots) — "effectiveness … not assessed." | p.115 ¶2 | Author assertion (un-evaluated) |
| 14 | Policy recommendations (selected, bolded): strengthen credit registry; alternative-data credit scoring for informal firms; specialised commercial courts; simplify SME stock-market access; open-finance data sharing; minimum reporting threshold reduction; upgrade card-payment regulation; eliminate cross-system uncertainty; school curriculum digital literacy; regulatory sandboxes; broadband competition; cash-rebate/lottery incentives to digital pay. | p.116–117, Table 2.2 | OECD recommendations, not enacted |

### Key qualifications preserved
- All digital-divide and payments data are **national statistics / surveys** (ENDUTIH, ENIF, ENAFIN, CNBV) **not** OECD modelling.
- Recommendations in Table 2.2 are **proposals**, not policy enacted by the AMLO administration.
- 2020 digital-ID measure and digital National Population Registry are **announced**, "not yet operative" — treat as **author assertion of intent**, not realisation.
- CoDi usage numbers (IFT 2021) describe **awareness/use among fixed-broadband users**, not population-wide.
- Period anchor: data mostly 2017–2020; some 2021 (CoDi survey, fraud stats); no later reforms discussed.

### Limitations / contrary material / reopen notes
- Extract focuses on **digital/finance access (Chapter 2)**, not the macroeconomic pillar (fiscal/debt/inflation — 5B.3) or competition/regulation (5B.4) sections; reopened chapters needed for those 5B questions.
- No primary government or Ministry of Finance text cited; revenue/capacity claims absent from this slice.
- MexicoX/@prende.mx "effectiveness not assessed" — claim flagged for verification, not adoption.
- Fintech authorisations: denominator ~76 mid-Oct 2021; status of conditional approvals after that date **unknown** in extract.
- "Mexico ranks last" in IoT M2M (Fig.2.25) is **rank among depicted OECD subset**, not all 38 OECD members — language rephrased cautiously.
- Author/institutional incentives not inferred beyond OECD's stated oversight mandate (Box 2.7 principles).

### 5B question coverage (this extract)
- **5B.6** infrastructure/admin capacity/regulation: strong coverage (digital govt, broadband, fintech reg, courts, ID).
- **5B.7** information, audit, correction: partial (PIAAC, ENIF/ENAFIN data, but no audit-institution review).
- **5B.8** distributional findings: rich (region, age, education, formal/informal, gender via "kinship tax").
- **5B.9** shock response: pandemic-accelerated digitalisation only.
- **5B.10** durable trajectory: implicit (skills agenda, digital identity pipeline), not explicit forecast.
- **5B.3 / 5B.4 / 5B.5:** outside this chunk; reopen with fiscal/chapter-1 and competition sections.

*Continuation flag:* Macro/competition chapters (5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.5) require separate OECD Survey chunk ingestion before chapter judgement.
